Approved under policy v2: REVIEW_APPROVED, for the full locked conjecture bounty.

The submission constructs a bijection of all natural numbers avoiding four-term arithmetic progressions in both increasing and decreasing value order along increasing indices, refuting the exact Erdős 196 target. The reviewed predicate includes both orientations; changing from positive integers to zero-based naturals is immaterial under translation.

A finite saturation argument and extension lemma yield nested finite stages that eventually contain every natural number. The proof establishes injectivity and surjectivity separately and proves unrestricted progression avoidance before constructing the final equivalence. No unproved extension assumption remains.

The inspected [SamuelSchlesinger research record](https://github.com/SamuelSchlesinger/erdos-problems/blob/9f18b1d6bb2c144761e47d304282f0ce3fec5631/research/permutation-monotone-ap/RESULTS.md) leaves its full permutation construction conditional on missing finite-feasibility or merge obligations. Its restricted results do not establish this target. [Geneson's introduction](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.12604v1) distinguishes its density results from an enumeration of all naturals avoiding four-term progressions; [LeSaulnier–Vijay](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0012365X10003936) impose an odd-difference restriction absent here. The retained comparison did not establish distinctive copied proof blocks.

The exact accepted proof and task passed production verification and a fresh isolated replay on 10 September 2026, including statement, dependency, permitted-axiom, and Lean-kernel checks. No material formalization defect or published disqualification reason was established by the recorded review. Under v2, unresolved provenance questions alone do not justify denying the reward. This is an eligibility decision, not a guarantee of originality. The verification replays used the Lean default kernel; an independent-kernel check was not performed.
